name: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2507.21046, submitted Jul 2025); accepted to Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), Jan 2026
authors_affiliation: Huan-ang Gao, Jiayi Geng, Wenyue Hua, Mengkang Hu, Xinzhe Juan, ... Cheng Qian, Qingyun Wu, Heng Ji, Mengdi Wang (27 authors, equal-contribution alphabetical order; corresponding: Hongru Wang and Mengdi Wang). Lead/primary affiliations: Princeton University & Princeton AI Lab; Tsinghua University; CMU; University of Sydney; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Penn State; University of Michigan; Oregon State; CUHK; Fudan; HKUST(GZ); HKU; UC Santa Barbara; UC San Diego; University of Edinburgh; UIUC.
code_url: N/A (no method code; this is a survey)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/CharlesQ9/Self-Evolving-Agents (official maintained awesome-list / paper collection, Apache-2.0, ~1.2k stars; last updated Oct 2025)
task_domain: Survey spanning agentic task domains: QA/reasoning, coding (SWE-bench, MLE-Bench), web/GUI navigation (WebArena, WebShop, Mind2Web, OSWorld, mobile), tool-use (ToolBench, API-Bank, T-Eval), embodied (Voyager/Minecraft), multi-agent, and specialized domains (education, healthcare, finance/quant trading, scientific discovery).
problem_setting: Survey of self-evolving LLM agents: systems that autonomously modify their internal parameters, contextual state, toolset, or architectural topology based on their own trajectories or feedback to improve future performance. Formalizes the agent system as a (multi-)agent tuple over a POMDP environment, with a self-evolving strategy f that recurrently maps (agent, trajectory, feedback) -> new agent to maximize cumulative utility over a task sequence. Covers offline and online/test-time settings, single- and multi-agent systems, with supervision ranging from scalar rewards to textual feedback; explicitly distinguishes passive (externally scheduled) vs active (self-initiated exploration/reflection) evolution and proto-evolution vs strong self-evolution.
what_is_retrieved: As a survey, it reviews what self-evolving components store/retrieve/reuse: long-term memory entries (episodic experiences, facts), distilled experiences/insights/guidelines/rules (Expel, AutoGuide, ReasoningBank), demonstrations/trajectories (cross-agent and self-generated), skills/tools/executable programs (Voyager, Alita), prompts/instructions, and retrieved cases (Memento case bank). Retrieval-augmented memory is one evolutionary locus among models, context, tools, architecture.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID across the surveyed field: emphasizes a GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes back to (Mem0, A-mem, SAGE, Memory-R1, Memento, ReasoningBank, Agent Workflow Memory) but also covers static external corpora/tools and tool indices; the survey's central axis is precisely the static-to-growing (online-growth/write-back) distinction.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a primary survey axis; the survey's optimization objective is maximizing cumulative utility of the evolving agent over a task sequence (continual improvement), not a fixed top-k retrieval ranking. It does cite completeness-oriented tool retrieval (COLT, ToolRet) as part of the tool-evolution discussion. [uncertain] as a unifying axis.
retrieval_unit: Surveyed across granularities: single memory record/fact, full trajectory and sub-trajectory, distilled insight/guideline/rule, free-text workflow/routine, executable skill/program, tool/API, prompt/instruction, and retrieved case (problem-solution). No single canonical unit since it is a survey.
index_source: Survey covers all three: offline-induced stores (STaR/bootstrapped data, ExpeL rules), online/test-time-induced growing memory (WebRL self-evolving curriculum, Mobile-Agent-E, Alita, Memento), and hybrid. The 'when to evolve' taxonomy (intra-test-time vs inter-test-time/offline vs online) directly organizes index-source timing.
index_structure_topology: Survey reviews flat vector memory, metadata/context-keyed memory, interconnected knowledge networks (A-mem Zettelkasten dynamic linking), hierarchical memory (G-Memory for multi-agent systems), and graph/workflow structures; architecture evolution covers graph/code topologies of agent systems.
retriever_type: Survey-level: covers off-the-shelf dense/similarity retrieval over memory, generative tool retrieval (ToolGen tool-as-token), LLM-as-retriever, and learned/RL retrieval policies (Memento, Memory-R1). No single retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: Survey reviews the spectrum: none/similarity top-k, RL/learned policy for memory and case selection (Memento online RL case-retrieval policy; Memory-R1 RL-trained Memory Manager; REMEMBER RL-updated experience memory), and reward/feedback-driven selection. A key surveyed shift is from fixed similarity retrieval to RL-optimized retrieval/memory-management policies.
query_construction: Not unified (survey). Reviews methods using raw task input, reflection/self-critique-conditioned queries, and learned memory triggers (MemGen learned memory trigger deciding when to invoke memory; Mem0 fact extraction from recent dialogue).
query_granularity: Survey covers task-level, trajectory-level, and step/state-level retrieval; the intra-test-time vs inter-test-time temporal taxonomy spans within-task (step-level) and across-task (trajectory/task-level) granularities.
when_to_retrieve: Survey-level: covers one-shot, iterative, and adaptive/learned triggers. The 'When to Evolve' chapter is a core axis: Intra-Test-Time (during task execution, real-time/active) vs Inter-Test-Time (between tasks, offline or online); learned memory triggers (MemGen) decide invocation.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Survey reviews fixed schedule, self-confidence/uncertainty, reflection/self-critique signals, environment feedback (scalar reward or textual), and learned triggers (MemGen memory trigger). The intra-test-time mode is characterized by the agent recognizing its own limitations and self-initiating learning.
reranking: Not a focal survey axis; reranking is implicit in retrieval-augmented memory discussion but not analyzed as a standalone dimension. [uncertain]
retrieved_context_refinement: Survey covers post-retrieval refinement via experience distillation (raw trajectories -> insights/rules in ExpeL, AutoGuide, ReasoningBank), summarization/tagging (MemInsight), and memory consolidation (ADD/MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE in Mem0). Distillation into general guidance rather than retrieving exact instances is highlighted as a key memory-evolution aspect.
how_retrieved_used: Survey-level: prompt augmentation (ICL with retrieved experiences/demos), skill reuse (Voyager skill library), case adaptation (Memento), latent-token injection (MemGen generative latent memory), and as training signal (RL/SFT on self-generated trajectories). Memory and experience are reused to shape future decision-making.
planning_integration: Survey reviews retrieval/experience integrated as one-shot exemplars at plan time, per-step interleaved reflection (Reflexion, AdaPlanner, Self-Refine), retrieve-then-plan over memory, and inside online RL loops (WebRL, RAGEN). Planning is one of the internal agent capabilities evaluated.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Survey spans per-answer, per-CoT-step (Self-Refine, Reflexion iterative refinement), and per-rollout interleaving; intra-test-time evolution couples adaptation tightly with each step of task execution.
retrieved_item_representation: Survey covers raw trajectories, distilled strategies/guidelines/rules (free text), free-text workflows (Agent Workflow Memory), executable skills/programs (Voyager, Alita), structured/tagged notes (MemInsight, A-mem), and latent/soft tokens (MemGen).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Survey explicitly contrasts retrieving raw past instances vs distilling experiences into more general guidance (insights, state-aware guidelines/rules in ExpeL/AutoGuide/ReasoningBank), reusable workflows, and procedural skills; this raw-vs-distilled abstraction spectrum is a discussed memory-evolution theme.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Survey discusses self-reflection/critique, verifier and reward models, and memory consolidation that deletes contradictions (Mem0 DELETE), plus notes 'Feedback Friction' (LLMs struggle to incorporate external feedback) as a challenge. Not formalized into a single robustness taxonomy. [uncertain]
memory_type: Survey taxonomy of memory/context as an evolutionary locus: episodic/long-term memory, skill-library, workflow/procedural memory, graph/interconnected memory (A-mem, G-Memory), and latent generative memory (MemGen). Context is one of four 'what-to-evolve' pillars (Models, Context, Tools, Architecture).
write_back: Yes (central theme). The survey frames self-evolving agents as systems that write back experiences/cases/skills: memory evolution where agents store, forget, and retrieve; Mem0 ADD/MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE; Memory-R1 RL Memory Manager; Memento evolving case bank; skill libraries (Voyager). Write-back/online-growth is an explicit organizing axis.
online_growth: Yes. The 'When to Evolve' chapter distinguishes inter-test-time online learning (continuous adaptation from streaming interaction data: WebRL self-evolving online curriculum, Mobile-Agent-E, Alita, DigiRL) and intra-test-time adaptation, vs frozen offline-induced stores. Online growth of the store during deployment is a first-class surveyed dimension.
write_back_trigger: Survey covers the spectrum: reflective writes after self-critique (Reflexion, ExpeL), on-success and on-failure storage, per-step/per-episode updates (REMEMBER updates memory after each episode), learned/RL-decided writes (Memory-R1, MemGen trigger), and human-validated. No single trigger.
failure_experience_usage: Survey notes both success and failure experiences are leveraged: agents reflect on failed trajectories (Reflexion verbal reinforcement from failures), distill corrective insights/rules, and consolidate/delete contradictory memories (Mem0). Contrastive use of success+failure is discussed within reflection/experiential-learning methods.
memory_evolution_update: Survey explicitly covers post-write dynamics: append-only accumulation, dedup-merge and delta-update (Mem0 ADD/MERGE/UPDATE/DELETE), forget-prune (SAGE Ebbinghaus forgetting curve), and link-and-evolve (A-mem dynamic indexing and linking forming knowledge networks). Memory mutation after writing is a discussed axis.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (surveyed). The survey highlights works where retrieval/case-selection/memory-management is a learned RL policy rather than fixed top-k: Memento (online RL case-retrieval policy, fine-tuning agents without fine-tuning the LLM), Memory-R1 (RL-trained Memory Manager selecting ADD/UPDATE/DELETE), REMEMBER (RL signals to update experience memory).
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes (surveyed). Covers cross-agent demonstration learning (Sec 5.2.2), multi-agent shared/hierarchical memory (G-Memory for multi-agent systems), self-evolving multi-agent collaboration networks, and the 'Ecosystems of Multi-Agents' future-direction chapter discussing co-evolution and shared experience across agents.
benchmarks: Catalogs many: SWE-bench, MLE-Bench, ScienceAgentBench, DSBench, WebArena, WebShop, Mind2Web/Mind2Web 2, OSWorld, WebWalker, BrowseComp, GAIA, AgentBench, LifelongAgentBench, TheAgentCompany, xbench, ToolBench/ToolLLM, API-Bank, T-Eval, ACEBench, Seal-Tools, MCP-Universe, MultiAgentBench, SwarmBench, Collab-Overcooked, Agent-SafetyBench, ST-WebAgentBench, AgentDAM, LTMBenchmark, PlanBench, ACPBench, StoryBench.
benchmark_family: Spans QA/reasoning, code (SWE-bench/MLE-Bench/ScienceAgentBench), web & GUI (WebArena/WebShop/Mind2Web/OSWorld/mobile), tool (ToolBench/API-Bank/T-Eval/MCP-Universe), embodied (Voyager/Minecraft), memory/lifelong (LifelongAgentBench/LTMBenchmark), multi-agent (MultiAgentBench/SwarmBench), and safety (Agent-SafetyBench/ST-WebAgentBench).
baselines: N/A as a survey (no head-to-head method baselines). It instead positions itself against prior surveys (e.g., 'A survey on self-evolution of large language models', 'Advances and challenges in foundation agents', 'Lifelong learning of LLM-based agents: a roadmap') and contrasts self-evolving agents with curriculum learning, lifelong/continual learning, model editing, and unlearning.
key_metrics: Survey proposes a five-goal evaluation framework with associated metrics: Adaptivity (e.g., Success Rate by Iteration Steps / learning curve), Retention (catastrophic-forgetting / knowledge stability), Generalization (in-domain-evolve / out-of-domain-evaluate transfer), Efficiency (cost-aware: tokens/latency/compute), and Safety. Notes shift from single-shot scoring to longitudinal, cost-aware trajectory metrics.
headline_result: N/A (survey, no single empirical headline number). Its headline contribution is the first systematic taxonomy organizing self-evolving agents along What / When / How / Where to evolve, plus a five-dimension (Adaptivity, Retention, Generalization, Efficiency, Safety) evaluation framework. 77 pages, 9 figures, ~455 references.
ablations: N/A (survey; no controlled ablations). Provides comparative tables instead: Table 2 (methods x four evolutionary pillars Model/Context/Tool/Architecture), Table 3 (How-to-evolve: feedback type/source, learning method, updated components, update timing), and evaluation coverage/gap tables (Tables 6-11).
evaluation_decoupling: Survey advocates decoupling: distinguishes Internal/Component-level evaluation (planning, tool use, memory management, multi-agent coordination) from External end-to-end task-solving evaluation, and separates static, short-horizon adaptive, and long-horizon lifelong assessment paradigms.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey argues for both: beyond final-outcome scoring it calls for trajectory-centric, process-aware, longitudinal assessment (adaptation over time, retention, step-wise component quality), criticizing single-shot outcome-only evaluation as insufficient for self-evolving agents.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Survey elevates Efficiency to one of five core evaluation goals (cost-aware assessment: token/compute/latency budgets, per-query token budgets, millisecond response constraints) and flags that current benchmarks under-evaluate adaptation under hard resource limits.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Discussed qualitatively under efficiency and architecture-under-operational-constraints (per-query token budgets, real-time latency limits) rather than via a fixed k recipe. [uncertain] as a concrete prescribed budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: Explicit organizing axes: What to evolve (Models, Context [memory + prompt], Tools, Architecture [single/multi-agent]); When to evolve (Intra-test-time vs Inter-test-time, offline vs online); How to evolve (reward-based, imitation/demonstration learning, population-based/evolutionary, plus cross-cutting dimensions); Where to evolve (general vs specialized domains: coding, education, healthcare, finance, science). Plus Evaluation (5 goals) and Future Directions. ~455 references; coverage window through 2025 (v4 revised Jan 2026). First systematic survey of self-evolving agents.
builds_on: Builds on prior agent and self-evolution literature: surveys on LLM agents and foundation agents; 'A survey on self-evolution of LLMs' (Tao et al. 2024); 'Lifelong learning of LLM-based agents: a roadmap'; and foundational methods it organizes (Reflexion, Self-Refine, ExpeL, Voyager, STaR, AFlow/ADAS, Mem0, AgentBench).
contrasts_with: Explicitly contrasted (Table 1) with related learning paradigms: curriculum learning, lifelong/continual learning, model editing, and unlearning, emphasizing self-evolving agents' adaptive, dynamic, and autonomous (active self-initiated) nature. Also distinguished from prior LLM-self-evolution surveys by focusing on agent-system-level evolution across components/timing/methods/domains.
lineage: Surveys lineage. A foundational taxonomy/roadmap survey for the self-evolving / experience-growing agent line; relevant to the write-back / online-growth axis separating experience-/memory-evolving agents from static RAG planners.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (survey, not a CBR method). It does review CBR-style methods within memory evolution (e.g., Memento's Retrieve-Reuse over an evolving case bank), but does not itself implement a CBR cycle.
explicit_cbr_grounding: No. The survey does not frame itself as case-based reasoning nor systematically cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; CBR mechanisms appear only implicitly via surveyed case-bank methods (e.g., Memento).
tool_document_engineering: Survey reviews tool evolution (creation/mastery/management) and tool retrieval/representation (ToolGen tool-as-token generation, ToolLLM, COLT completeness-oriented tool retrieval, ToolRet benchmark) but does not prescribe a single document-engineering recipe.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Survey covers dynamic/live tool ecosystems and protocols, including MCP (MCP-Universe benchmark) and RapidAPI-based tool stores (ToolBench/ToolLLM 16000+ APIs), and discusses self-directed tool discovery/integration lifecycle (Alita) as an under-evaluated capability.
tool_dependency_awareness: Survey acknowledges tool ecosystems and multi-API planning (AppBench planning of multiple APIs) but inter-tool dependency modeling is not a dedicated analyzed axis. [uncertain]
adaptation_mechanism: Survey covers adaptation/reuse mechanisms across methods: verbatim ICL exemplars, LLM-prompted/reflective revision (Reflexion, Self-Refine, AdaPlanner), execution-feedback-driven revision, RL reuse/fine-tuning (Memento, RAGEN), and latent adaptation (MemGen). Not a single mechanism (survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (survey, not a benchmark). It catalogs and analyzes benchmark coverage gaps (Tables 7-8) rather than constructing a dataset.
